newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's new premier yet to win full acceptance.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's new premier yet to win full acceptance.

text.p: Cambodia's new first prime minister Ung Huot faces some hurdles before winning full acceptance, political analysts said on Wednesday.
King Norodom Sihanouk's approval is seen as crucial.

More than two thirds of members in the 120-seat National Assembly voted on Wednesday in favour of Foreign Minister Ung Huot's nomination to replace Prince Norodom Ranariddh, ousted by his co-premier Hun Sen a month ago.
"It's another step but more things have to be done," said an Asian diplomat. "The question is whether this is accepted by the king or not."

King Sihanouk, father of Ranariddh, said late last month he would not recognise Ung Huot as first premier as the post belonged to his son. The king also said a vote on a new first prime minister by an incomplete parliament would be invalid.

The Cambodian constitution requires the king's approval of a new first prime minister. Hun Sen told reporters on Wednesday that he and Ung Huot were preparing to visit Sihanouk soon in Beijing, where he is receiving medical treatment.
"There are still some major constitutional hurdles which Ung Huot has not yet jumped including the approval of the king," said another diplomat.
"This may be an attempt to gloss things over but we have to ask the question, do we put any store by this constitution or not?" he said.

"There's also the question of whether FUNCINPEC can really be seen, in all honesty, to be an independent party," said the diplomat, referring to Ranariddh's royalist party whose depleted ranks nominated Ung Huot.
A Cambodian political analyst said the fact that Ung Huot won the ballots of 86 of the 99 members in parliament on Wednesday added weight to his claim for recognition.

"Any procedure is bound to have complications," he said of the constitutional requirements not met on Wednesday. "But the secret ballot should overcome those complications to some extent. It was not against the will of the MPs."
"The king can't say no, it was a secret ballot. In my view he'll have to approve whether he likes it or not," he said.
The United States and the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) both said after the prince's ouster on July 6 that they still recognised the prince as first prime minister.
The United States said Ung Huot's nomination by a depleted FUNCINPEC party was not acceptable.

Many of Ranariddh's supporters fled the country in the wake of Hun Sen's bloody takeover and a subsequent crackdown on the FUNCINPEC party in which some 40 people were killed, according to estimates by United Nations human rights officials.
Among those who fled were some 20 members of parliament from Ranariddh's party and a smaller allied party.
Most of them went to Bangkok where on Wednesday the Cambodian opposition condemned Ung Huot's approval as first prime minister as illegal and a violation of the constitution.

"The appointment today by the National Assembly in an atmosphere of intimidation and fear of Mr Ung Huot is totally illegal," the Union of Cambodian Democrats opposition group said in a statement released in the Thai capital.
Earlier on Wednesday the National Assembly voted by show of hands to strip Ranariddh of his parliamentary immunity paving the way for his prosecution if he returns to Cambodia.
Hun Sen has ruled out negotiating with Ranariddh and said he must face trial for conducting illegal negotiations with the Khmer Rouge guerrilla group and for alleged weapons smuggling.
Ranariddh has dismissed the accusations and called from abroad for opposition to Hun Sen.
